## Excercise

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
library(haven)
TEDS_2016 <- read_stata("https://github.com/datageneration/home/blob/master/DataProgramming/data/TEDS_2016.dta?raw=true")
regplot <- function(x, y, var_name = "Variable") {
  # Remove NAs so the model and plot align
  df_clean <- na.omit(data.frame(x = x, y = y))
  
  fit <- lm(y ~ x, data = df_clean)

  plot(jitter(df_clean$x), jitter(df_clean$y), 
       pch = 19, 
       col = rgb(0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 0.3), # Transparent blue
       xlab = var_name, 
       ylab = "Dependent Variable (Tondu)",
       main = paste("Regression: Tondu vs", var_name))
  abline(fit, col = "red", lwd = 3)
  
  return(summary(fit))
}

# a. Age
age_summary <- regplot(TEDS_2016$age, TEDS_2016$Tondu, "Age")

# b. Education
edu_summary <- regplot(TEDS_2016$edu, TEDS_2016$Tondu, "Education")

# c. Income
inc_summary <- regplot(TEDS_2016$income, TEDS_2016$Tondu, "Income")

# 5. Multiple Regression (to improve prediction)
multiple_model <- lm(Tondu ~ age + edu + income, data = TEDS_2016)
summary(multiple_model)
```

# Problem

The problem lies in doing linear regression analysis on discrete/categorical data. Using a different strategy (such as a generalized linear model) would better fit the distribution of data).
